name: lodash-minby-iteratee-poker-hands
behavioral_change: lodash v4.0.0 split the iteratee-accepting forms of `_.max` and `_.min` into `_.maxBy` and `_.minBy`; `_.min` no longer accepts an iteratee and silently ignores the second argument, comparing elements directly. The name, arity and call form are unchanged and no exception is thrown.
downstream_effect: The downstream project calls `_.min(tiebreakers, getValueIndex)` in index.js:135 to pick the strongest card by its index in `cardOrder`; after the upgrade the card strings are compared directly, so the public method `judgeWinner` silently returns the wrong winner. The single failure is a should assertion ("expected Array [ 0, 0, 1, 0, 1 ] to equal Array [ 1, 0, 1, 0, 0 ]") whose only frame is test.js:72; lodash, index.js, `_.min`, minBy and getValueIndex never appear.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in index.js:135 from `_.min(tiebreakers, getValueIndex)` to `_.minBy(tiebreakers, getValueIndex)`.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog for v4.0.0 (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog#v400), Compatibility Warnings section, states "Split `_.max` & `_.min` into `_.maxBy` & `_.minBy`" and includes a before/after code block (`_.min(objects, 'a')` in 3.10.1 versus `_.minBy(objects, 'a')` in 4.0.0), which shows the new code form.
failing_tests: test.js :: poker > .judgeWinner(hands) should return the index of the winning hand
